sngl:ui

sngl:ui The user interface: the components most applications are built from, and the vocabulary they share. What is here is the portable core -- a `button` means the same thing on the web, on a phone, in a desktop toolkit and in a terminal, and a platform that renders it differently still renders the same declaration. Specialized surfaces live in packages under this one, so that a program pays for a drawing canvas or a document viewer only by importing it: sngl:ui/draw a canvas and the 2D shapes it hosts The components fall into five groups: display show a value and do not edit it form controls the user edits, each with a two-way bound value prop layout containers, which place their children nav move the user somewhere else overlay paint above the rest of the tree `node` is the family all five belong to, and `window` is the surface they are placed on -- the one member of `root`, the family a package body accepts. The two are here rather than in an application-shell package of their own because a window is where widgets go: what it hosts is `node`, so any package holding it would import this one and be imported back. `Style`, the style enums and the units sit here rather than in a package of their own because every component in every one of those packages refers to them; they are the vocabulary, not a separate concern. Nothing here is in scope until it is imported. `import <alias> "sngl:ui"` qualifies its declarations (`alias.vbox`), and is also how a platform overrides a component (`component <alias>.vbox`); it is the form this repository writes. `import . "sngl:ui"` writes them unqualified and remains supported. Components
  • avatar A user's picture, or `fallback` where there is none to show: no source was given, or the one given failed to load.
  • badge Small status label — a compact chip showing a status, count, or category tag.
  • button Clickable button that triggers an action, labeled with `text`.
  • card Styled container for grouping related content.
  • checkbox Boolean toggle rendered as a checkmark box.
  • chip Compact interactive tag.
  • choice One of a select's choices: data, since it names itself as its family, so a select reads its choices as a list rather than rendering them.
  • datepicker Calendar-based date selection.
  • divider Visual separator line.
  • drawer Slide-out panel anchored to a side of the viewport.
  • file A file shipped with the program.
  • hbox Horizontal box layout container.
  • image Shows the picture its source holds, scaled into its frame by `fit` -- what html's `<picture>` is.
  • imageSource Where an image's pixels come from.
  • input Single-line text input field.
  • link Navigational hyperlink.
  • menu Context or dropdown menu.
  • menuItem One entry of a menu or a menu bar: data, since it names itself as its family, so the menu reads its entries as a list rather than rendering them.
  • menubar Horizontal menu bar — typically at the top of a window on desktop.
  • modal Dialog overlay.
  • node The family the widgets form: a button, a label and a layout box are members of it, and any of them goes anywhere another does.
  • popover Floating content panel anchored to a trigger.
  • progress Progress indicator, showing the fraction `value / max` filled.
  • radio Group of mutually exclusive options.
  • remote An image fetched while the program runs, from a URL.
  • scroll Scrollable viewport that wraps a single child.
  • select Dropdown selection control.
  • spacer Flexible empty space: it grows into the room its siblings leave along its parent's axis, as `flex: 1` does in CSS, which is the common way to right-align content in an `hbox`.
  • spinner Indeterminate loading indicator.
  • splitview Resizable two-pane layout.
  • stack Layered container where children overlap in the order they are declared.
  • tab One tab of a `tabs`: data, since it names itself as its family, so the tabs read their tabs as a list rather than rendering them.
  • table Tabular data display.
  • tableRow One of a table's rows: data, since it names itself as its family, so a table reads its rows as a list rather than rendering them.
  • tabs Tabbed navigation.
  • text Displays a text string.
  • textarea Multi-line text input field.
  • toggle On/off switch control.
  • toolbar Horizontal bar of controls: its children, a mix of buttons, separators and spacers, each answering for itself.
  • tooltip Informational popup on hover or focus.
  • tree Hierarchical data display.
  • treeItem One node of a tree: data, since it names itself as its family, so a tree reads its nodes as a list rather than rendering them.
  • vbox Vertical box layout container.
  • window A top-level window — a surface the user sees, which a program creates and destroys with the tree.

  • Style Declarative style properties applied via the `style` prop on any visual component.

    • Enums
  • Alignment Cross-axis alignment of children inside a flex container.
  • AvatarVariant The outline an avatar is clipped to.
  • BorderStyle Line style drawn along a component's border.
  • Display Intrinsic layout mode.
  • FlexDirection Main-axis direction for flex containers such as `vbox` and `hbox`.
  • FontStyle Slant applied to fonts.
  • FontWeight Numeric weight for fonts.
  • InputType What an input field holds, which a platform may answer with a keyboard, masking or validation of its own.
  • Justification Main-axis distribution of children inside a flex container.
  • LinkTarget Where a followed link opens: in place of the current view, or in a new window.
  • ListStyle Marker style for list-rendered containers.
  • ObjectFit How an `image`'s contents are sized to fit its frame.
  • Orientation The axis a group of controls is laid out along.
  • Overflow Behavior when content exceeds its container's bounds.
  • Position Positioning scheme for a component within its parent's layout flow.
  • SizePreset A preset size for a component that offers three.
  • SortDirection Which way a table's sorted column runs, if it is sorted at all.
  • SpinnerVariant The shape a spinner turns in.
  • TabsVariant How a tab strip marks the selected tab.
  • TextAlign Horizontal alignment of inline text content.
  • WhiteSpace Whether a host collapses runs of whitespace in a component's text, and where it may break a line.
